title: Surface Graph (Random-Surfer Reader Model Input)
description: A reading/interaction graph for scripts/surfer_model.mjs. Covers web flows, wireframes, PDF documents, and LaTeX books with one shape. Every field is a number, boolean, or explicit concept label the analyst decided while reading the surface: the script performs no text, image, or URL inspection. Node order IS reading order — index 0 is where a linear reader starts.

surfaceKind.description: What is being audited. Changes which findings are meaningful, not the arithmetic. See references/surface-adapters.md for how to encode each kind, and what each kind CANNOT tell you.

readerMode.description: Which surfer to run. Reader modes are parameter presets on one chain, not separate models: skim teleports often and abandons fast, study reads linearly and re-reads. Run a document in ALL of skim/scan/study — a surface that only survives 'study' has an acquisition problem, because nobody starts in study mode.

workingSetWindowNodes.description: How many nodes back a freshly-introduced concept still counts against working memory. Counted in nodes, so size nodes to one reading sitting (a section, a screen, a page spread). Raise this only if your nodes are unusually fine-grained.

patienceBudget.description: How long this reader will actually give the surface before the decision to continue is re-made from scratch. Used to gate total reading time and time-to-first-insight.

rationale.description: Where the number came from — a real telemetry figure, a stated reading occasion, or an assumption. Say which.

entryNodes.description: Where surfers arrive, with optional weights. A book entered only at its cover models a very different reader from one entered at a search hit in Chapter 6 — model both. Defaults to the first node.

payoffNodes.description: The nodes that actually deliver the value the surface promises: the result, the working feature, the answer. Reach probability and time-to-first-insight are computed against these. A surface with no declared payoff node has not been analysed, only described.

readerPaths.description: Prescribed routes through the surface, one per named kind of reader - the book's own "Reader's Map" or "How to read this book", or a docs site's role-based tracks. Each route is evaluated as its own surface: the same chain, restricted to the prescribed nodes in the prescribed order. That is what catches a map whose route skips the chapter introducing a concept the route later needs - a defect the linear reading order hides completely.

id.description: Stable identifier for the route, used in finding messages.

label.description: The route as the document names it, e.g. "Practitioner track".

persona.description: The vocational identity this route is written for, matched to a persona in product-appeal-analyzer's spec. A route with no persona is a route nobody was chosen for; a persona with no route is a reader the map forgot.

nodes.description: Node ids in the order the map prescribes. Need not be contiguous - skipping is the point.

readerMode.description: Override the graph's reader mode for this route. A practitioner track is usually read in scan or skim mode even when the book as a whole is a study read.

patienceBudgetSeconds.description: This reader's budget, which is usually not the book's. A practitioner track promising four hours to someone with one is a broken promise even if every chapter on it is excellent.

payoffNodes.description: What pays THIS reader, if different from the document's overall payoff. Defaults to the graph's payoffNodes that lie on the route; an empty result is itself a finding.

nodes.description: Reading positions in reading order: screens in a flow, frames in a wireframe, sections in a document, chapters/sections in a book.

label.description: Human-readable name, used verbatim in findings.

kind.description: What this node is. Documentary only today, but it keeps a graph legible to the next analyst.

costSeconds.description: Expected seconds to read/complete this node once. For prose, estimate from word count at the reader's real rate (roughly 200-250 wpm for ordinary prose, and far slower for dense technical text — 50-100 wpm is common for mathematics).

newConcepts.description: Concepts, terms, or notation this node INTRODUCES (defines, names, or explains for the first time). The label is an arbitrary stable string; only identity across nodes matters.

requiresConcepts.description: Concepts this node leans on to be understood. A concept required here but introduced nowhere is a dangling prerequisite; required here but introduced LATER is a forward reference. Both cost the reader, and the model charges for both.

payoff.description: How much of the surface's promised value this node actually delivers, 0-1. Lowers the abandon hazard: readers who are being paid keep reading.

hook.description: How strongly this node's ending pulls the reader onward, 0-1: an open question, a cliffhanger result, a visible next step. Distinct from payoff — a hook promises, a payoff delivers.

attentionElements.description: How many things compete for attention here at once: choices, fields, callouts, animated elements, marginalia, simultaneous figures. Measured against a working-memory limit of 4.

gestalt.description: The analyst's Gestalt judgement of this node, 0-10 each (10 = ideal). See references/gestalt-operators.md for the detection rules behind each score. Omitted sub-scores default to 10 (no penalty) so a partially-scored graph still runs.

groupingClarity.description: Do proximity/similarity/enclosure produce the groups the CONTENT actually has? 0 = the layout groups things that are unrelated and separates things that belong together.

figureGroundClarity.description: Does the primary thing separate cleanly from its background/chrome? 0 = everything has equal visual weight and nothing reads as primary.

continuityClarity.description: Does the layout imply the reading order the content needs (alignment, flow lines, a single dominant axis)? Recorded for reporting; not yet weighted in the hazard.

commonRegionClarity.description: Do enclosures/cards/rules bound exactly one idea each? Recorded for reporting; not yet weighted in the hazard.

links.description: Outgoing transitions in the reader's likely order. A node with NO links is terminal: reaching its end counts as finishing the surface. Backward links need not be listed — regression is derived from prerequisite distance.

kind.description: What kind of move this is. Documentary today.

weight.description: Relative likelihood among this node's outgoing links. Weights are normalised, so only ratios matter.
